assessments.reasoning: N3220 §6.2.5 paragraph 11, printed page 39 (PDF page 52), specifies the unsigned range through 2 to the power N minus 1 and describes arithmetic in that unsigned type as modulo 2 to the power N. Section 6.2.6.2 paragraph 1 defines width N as the number of value bits in the unsigned integer type. The exact bytes were retrieved from WG14's document directory and the PDF identifies itself as working draft N3220. The independently computed SHA-256 equals the registered digest.

challenge.method: Compare the arithmetic clause to the width definition and the promotions in §6.3.1.1. Challenge the candidate with an unsigned operand that promotes to int and with padding bits in the object representation.
challenge.results: The width in the modulus counts value bits. The promotion rules allow some unsigned operands to be converted to int when its range permits, so operand declaration alone does not establish the effective arithmetic type. The candidate expressly restricts its rule to arithmetic performed in the unsigned type.

limitations: The result describes unsigned integer arithmetic in N3220. Effective type after conversions, signed arithmetic, and implementation behavior have their own rules.
